evidence_rationale: F0 is the cheapest rung of the RQ-26 kill ladder (research/2026/b70-hq4-format-design-20261009.md section 4) and can close the question with zero GPU. RL-153 (operator decision D3) re-entered the question after RL-151 proved the RL-150 block-output KL degenerate on 4/6 blocks (every arm AND EXL3 read |KL| <= 4e-12; the residual pass-through saturates the standardized softmax) and after RL-150's AutoRound at iters=10 escaped every tensor to INT8. This plan fixes exactly what the registry changed_variable names: primary = KL on the block delta (the shared input cancels exactly, exposing the arm's full perturbation), secondary = final-logit KL through the real tail on 2 blocks, a mandatory RTN-INT3 sanity control that must clear KL > 1e-6 on every block before the campaign and any scoring, and AutoRound at the mandated 100 iterations with the deadline sized from a measured 1-tensor probe (scripts/tmp/rq26_ar_probe_20261011.py: 0.8295/1.3601 s/iter per 89.1M-param tensor at 2 threads, plus a synthetic-xs divergence diagnostic that motivates but does not change the mandated recipe). Arms, blocks, split, seeds, gates and ranking are unchanged from RL-150; identities are re-verified (farms, states re-verified 2026-10-11; states NOT regenerated). The same stop rule applies: a failed F0 after one rounding-recipe retry closes HQ4 for this model and records the measured KL gap as the value of the trellis. Measured probe arithmetic also shows the mandated campaign (~25,600 2-thread-job-seconds) exceeds the 3600 s screen budget on this 8-core host (~1.3-2.3x); the driver therefore carries a hard internal 6840 s deadline (5% margin) under the RL-155 budget accommodation that raised the screen cap to 7200 s before the sealed run — no gate, arm, iteration or recipe change — and schedules the campaign block-major so a truncated partial retains complete blocks.
